checks.recomputed: Checked against generator.py gen_night. Category is balanced(...) per block; seeds and all NIGHT_FACTORS use weighted_balanced with fixed counts per block and independent shuffles; model_mix is iid through core_params; tech lead is iid Bernoulli(0.5) on frng. Within-block permutation is therefore the exact randomization distribution, conditional on the counts. Labels are permuted per config and mapped to runs, also in the logistic test. The two-sided p counts ties as extreme. Replicate drift uses a sign flip within configs, which is the right pairing. No model selection or leakage is involved. DeLong correctly marked not applicable.

method_problems: The freeze verdict depends on analysis choices, not on Monte Carlo error. Holm-14 = 0.0533 +- 0.0005 is reliably above 0.05. But an equally valid statistic that weights configs by their runs (the permutation is still at config level, so the test stays exact) gives p = 0.0018 (Holm-14 <= 0.025). The block-stratified difference gives p = 0.0057 (Holm 0.063). Their equal-weight choice is sound and was stated up front: with ICC 0.73, inverse-variance weights for 1/2/3 runs are about 1/1.16/1.22. So this is a fragility to report, not an error.

Holm family. The 14-factor family is defensible because the FINDINGS sentences were picked after seeing all factors, but it is the most conservative option. Over the 5 FINDINGS comparisons, freeze gets Holm 0.0097. DECISIONS.md s.15 also pre-stated freeze as the base-rate dial with a direction ('Regler: ohne Freeze ~0 %'); the one-sided p is 0.0030. The adjusted tests are weaker (OLS +19.2 pp, p 0.031; logistic p 0.049), so 'partly supported / borderline' is a fair label. The text should say 'Holm p = 0.053, just above the line', not suggest a clear miss.

Monte Carlo resolution. With B = 10,000, the smallest p-values rest on 3-6 exceedances (0.0004-0.0007). My 50,000-permutation values are about half as large (discoverability 0.00018, channels 0.00030, category 0.00046), so their Holm values of 0.0056-0.0084 for these factors are conservative. Conclusions are unchanged. The report also mixes resolutions: the main table shows freeze p 0.0056 / Holm 0.0616 (10k), while the bottom line uses 0.00484 / 0.0532 (100k). The 100k value is the accurate one (2M permutations: 0.00484).
